CAN controller clock (the crystal, resonator or oscillator each controller takes)

values.value: R2 states each controller's clock tolerance, which the 1 Mbit/s bit rate depends on
values.source: Research.md:309 (R2 row), citing shared/can/include/can_timing.h:17-21 (requires the bit rate exact)
values.refutation_tried: Checked against IOBoard.md:168 (Bit timing: exactly 1 Mbit/s) and IOBoard.md:199 (Controller clock: makes 1 Mbit/s exactly). The controller's clock accuracy sets whether the nominal bit time comes out exact, so the row's framing holds.

values.value: each MCP2518FDT-E/SL, the link's and the external CAN port's, takes a 40 MHz clock (owner, 2026-10-01)
values.source: IOBoard.md:199 (Controller clock row); reason at hardware/docs/Pins.md:160-161: the MCP2518FD limits its SPI clock to 0.85 x SYSCLK / 2, so the link's 10 MHz SPI needs a 40 MHz system clock
values.refutation_tried: 0.85 x 40 / 2 = 17 MHz >= the 10 MHz SPI rate the link uses (IOBoard.md:200, Controller interface). Arithmetic supports 40 MHz as sufficient, but a lower frequency (e.g. 24 MHz, giving 10.2 MHz) would also clear that bound, so the specific 40 MHz figure is the owner's choice, not the only value the arithmetic forces. Consistent, not refuted.

values.quantity: whether the clock's frequency tolerance is stated
values.value: the CAN bit rate is exact to the controller's clock; the tolerance of the RP2354B's crystal and of the CAN controllers' clock is not stated; R1 and R2 state them
values.source: IOBoard.md:141 (Clock accuracy row), citing docs/DShot.md:221-230, docs/Link.md:196-209, shared/can/include/can_timing.h:17-21
values.refutation_tried: can_timing.h:17-21 requires an exact bit rate and states two nodes 1% apart fail on long frames, but gives no numeric ppm budget per node. This absence is already captured as V26 (Research.md:722) and V27 (Research.md:723) under Raised by P1, both answered 'for research' (owner, 2026-09-28): the owner has already assigned deriving the ppm limit to research rather than supplying a number, so this gap is not a new question for this follow-up.

values.value: for research (owner, 2026-09-28) -- no ppm figure given; only the 1% two-node long-frame failure point is stated
values.source: Research.md:722, V26 under Raised by P1
values.refutation_tried: Confirmed V26 is already in the Raised by P1 table with an owner answer ('for research'), so it is a question already raised, not re-raised here; it is the value P2 must derive before qualifying a crystal/oscillator part, and the owner has already directed that derivation to research rather than to itself.

values.quantity: largest frequency error of the external CAN controller's clock (ppm), including temperature and ageing
